requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a `habeas-requirements` skill whose description tells agents to use it during design sessions and before changing code, tests, or requirement text in a Habeas project, including when the user asks for a feature, bug fix, or other change without mentioning requirements.
rationale:
The requirement `requirements.cli.requirements_skill` has two testable obligations. Habeas must bundle a skill named `habeas-requirements`. Its description must tell agents to use it during design sessions and before changing code, tests, or requirement text. That includes when the user asks for a feature, bug fix, or other change without mentioning requirements.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_is_used_for_design_and_before_any_change]` is marked `{test}` for the requirement. It reads the front-matter description of the bundled `habeas-requirements` skill. It does this through the helpers `description`, `skill_md` and `skill_files`, which load `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` with `include_str!`. It then asserts that the description contains three phrases:

- "Use during design sessions and before changing code, tests, or requirement text in a project that tracks requirements with Habeas". This covers the design-session and before-any-change trigger, and the three change targets: code, tests and requirement text.
- "even when the user only asks for a feature, bug fix,". This covers the case where the user asks for a feature, bug fix or other change.
- "and never says \"requirement\"". This covers the case where the user does not mention requirements.

The bundling obligation is covered because `skill_files` maps the `habeas-requirements` name to the skill's `SKILL.md` at compile time. A missing skill file would fail the build, and a missing or empty `description:` line would panic in `description`.

I found no input class the text distinguishes that these assertions would miss. A description that dropped any of the required triggers would fail the matching phrase assertion. The search also showed the real `SKILL.md` front matter beginning "Use during design sessions and before changing code, tests, or requirement text...", which matches the asserted phrases.

text: Habeas MUST bundle a `habeas-requirements` skill whose description tells agents to use it during design sessions and before changing code, tests, or requirement text in a Habeas project, including when the user asks for a feature, bug fix, or other change without mentioning requirements.
